description: Operational artifact topology contract for the fixed workspace-owned run tree. Physical paths are extracted from the CLI planner so documentation and storage can refer to semantic roles instead of guessing from directory names.
isolation_note: Every run is a self-contained namespaced tree. Immutable workspace assets may be materialized into run.inputs, but the run records their identities in assets.lock.json and never writes into the shared object store.

isolation_models.isolated_run_tree: Each run owns its mutable configuration, inputs, output, logs, scheduler state, and manifest.
isolation_models.shared_content_addressed: Immutable objects are shared by digest and only read or materialized by runs.

default_layout_note: The workspace and run skeletons are fixed. YAML may select what is generated, but it cannot redirect mutable run output to peer diagnostics or results directories. Imported or generated reusable inputs live in the workspace asset store and are materialized into the run-owned inputs tree.

resolved_safety_history.note: Defects that were found and closed. Kept because the enforcement they produced is only intelligible next to the failure that motivated it, and because a reader needs to know the guard is deliberate rather than incidental. The configurable output/log topology that made this defect reachable has since been removed entirely; the guards it produced remain as defense in depth. Nothing here is an open defect.

entries.was: monitor io.directories.log is passed through to -log_dir with no containment validation, and on a fresh solve the C runtime calls PetscRMTree on that directory, recursively deleting it and its contents.
observed: picurv_cli/core.py emitted '-log_dir <value>' verbatim from monitor io.directories.log.
An absolute path outside the run tree was ACCEPTED by picurv validate and by run --dry-run (rc=0, no warning).
The dry-run planner reported <run>/logs regardless, so the configured destination was not visible in the plan.
entries.consequence: An accepted configuration can cause the solver to recursively delete an arbitrary directory, including one shared by other runs or holding unrelated data.

resolution.approach: First, picurv rejected io.directories.log and io.directories.output values that escaped the run directory, targeted the run root, named a reserved directory, or overlapped each other, with io.directories.allow_unsafe_paths waiving exactly one verdict; src/setup.c independently classified the log directory immediately before PetscRMTree. Then the surface itself was removed: run-owned directory names are fixed by the workspace contract, io.directories is no longer part of the monitor schema, and no override waives anything. The classifier and the C guard are both retained as defense in depth against a hand-edited or older staged control.
implementation: src/setup.c::LogDirectoryIsSafeToWipe (applies the waiver to one verdict)
picurv_cli/core.py::CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS (the canonical values preflight compares against)
resolution.residual_risk: The restart input is deliberately not containment-checked as a destination: it is a read path materialized from a validated source. The C guard classifies the log directory it is handed, so a simulator invoked by hand with a non-canonical -log_dir is protected by that guard alone, not by preflight. And nothing here establishes that the retained classifier and guard agree with the canonical set under every future layout change; the canonical values are asserted in one place, CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS, and both readers derive from it.
enforcement_points: reserved-flag rejection across case, solver, and monitor passthrough
dry-run planner (reports what a real run would refuse)
submission preflight over the staged .control file
the C runtime guard immediately before PetscRMTree, independent of the launcher
rejected_conditions: any run-owned directory flag whose value is not the canonical one (never waivable)
a value starting with '~', which nothing expands
escapes the run tree by relative traversal
resolves to the run root itself
resolves to a directory CONTAINING the run root, up to the filesystem root
a relative name that resolves outside the tree through a symlink
collides with a reserved run directory (config, scheduler, checkpoints, visualization)
log and output overlap, including against a defaulted value
directory values that cannot be written to a PETSc options line unambiguously (whitespace, quotes, comment markers)
an absolute location outside the run tree - formerly the one waivable condition, now refused like the rest
resolution.shared_rule_set: Configuration validation and submission preflight both call evaluate_run_directories() over effective values with defaults applied, so the two cannot drift apart and both honour the override identically.
resolution.parser_contract: Staged control files are tokenized with shlex, matching PETSc's treatment of a double-quoted span as one token. Splitting on whitespace read '-log_dir "/tmp/VICTIM DIR"' as the value '"/tmp/VICTIM', which looks contained while PETSc would use the absolute path. Malformed quoting is a preflight error, never a skipped line.
resolution.superseded_surface: io.directories and io.directories.allow_unsafe_paths were removed from the monitor schema with the fixed workspace topology. evaluate_run_directories() is still called by staged-control preflight, which now passes override=False unconditionally.
resolution.verdict_rule: Waivability was decided on a typed verdict, never on message text; with the waiver removed, every verdict is terminal. The typed classification is retained because the C guard still consumes it.
